## Messages

LiteRT-LM has its own `Message` and `Content` classes.
[`_mk_content`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_mk_content)
turns a string, bytes or a `Path` into the right content type, telling
image from audio by the bytes themselves or by the file extension.
[`_mk_msg`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_mk_msg) and
[`_mk_msgs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_mk_msgs)
build whole messages from those.

``` python
import tempfile
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
```

``` python
test_eq(_mk_msg("hello").to_json(), {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "hello"}]})
test_eq(_mk_msg("hi", role="model").to_json()["role"], Role.MODEL.value)
test_eq(_mk_msg("hi", role="assistant").role, Role.MODEL)   # either spelling, whichever litert-lm names it
test_eq([x["role"] for x in _mk_msgs(["a", _mk_msg("b", role="model")])], ["user", Role.MODEL.value])
assert isinstance(_mk_content("x"), Text)
# bytes are sniffed: image vs audio
assert isinstance(_mk_content(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + b'\x00'*16), ImageBytes)
assert isinstance(_mk_content(b'RIFF\x00\x00\x00\x00WAVE' + b'\x00'*16), AudioBytes)
```

## Portable history

rishi’s history is a list of OpenAI-shaped dicts, while LiteRT-LM speaks
its own `Message` objects and calls the assistant `model`. `fmt2hist`
converts LiteRT-LM messages into history dicts, and `hist2fmt` converts
them back. That is what lets a conversation started here continue on
llama.cpp or a hosted model through `messages=`, and the reverse. Images
and audio from earlier turns become `[image]` and `[audio]` placeholders
on the way into the history.

## LiteRT callbacks

Urai’s chats run callbacks at fixed points in a turn. LiteRT-LM needs
its own versions of three of them, because the engine keeps the
conversation itself.
[`_HistoryCallback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_historycallback)
copies each message and reply into `chat.hist` in the shared format.
[`_UsageCallback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_usagecallback)
works out token usage from how much the conversation’s `token_count`
grew during the turn.
[`_ToolReminderCallback`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#_toolremindercallback)
appends a short reminder of the available tools to the outgoing message.

## Tool calling

LiteRT-LM runs the tool loop inside the engine. The other local backends
run it in rishi. The engine calls your Python function and feeds the
result back to the model.
[`ChatToolHandler`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#chattoolhandler)
connects that loop to the chat. Before each call it runs the chat’s
`before_tool_calls` callbacks, checks the tool-call budget, and asks the
chat’s `approve` function if there is one. A refused call is recorded
with its reason instead of running. The handler writes each call and its
result into `chat.hist`, and runs the `after_tool_calls` callbacks after
each result. Approval itself is described on Urai’s
[chat](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/chat.html) page.

Several chats can share one engine. The engine runs one generation at a
time.
[`engine_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#engine_lock)
returns the single lock of an engine, and a chat holds it for the length
of a turn. The chat releases it while a tool runs, and the tool can use
the engine. Chats on other threads wait their turn. A second chat on the
same thread cannot wait, because the thread that holds the lock would
never release it. That chat raises
[`EngineBusy`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#enginebusy)
at once.

[`EngineHold`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#enginehold)
is that hold for one send. Use it as a context manager, or call `take`
and `let_go`.
[`ChatToolHandler`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#chattoolhandler)
calls `let_go` while a tool runs and `take` after it. A chat that
already holds the engine on this thread can take it again.
`recover_context` and a one-shot call from a callback do this. The lock
is a plain `Lock`, so closing a stream abandoned on another thread frees
the engine. The old name `_Hold` still works.

## Loading models and LitertChat

A `.litertlm` repo may hold several builds: a portable one, and others
made for one kind of hardware, whose names contain `-gpu`, `-npu`,
`-web` or an underscore.
[`get_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#get_model)
prefers the portable build. Searches of the repository exclude file
names that contain `web`. An existing `model_path` bypasses that filter.
It finds the file in three steps. It uses a `model_path` you pass if the
file exists. Otherwise it uses a portable build in the local Hugging
Face cache. Otherwise it downloads a build, and uses a hardware-specific
cached build only when the repo has no portable build or the Hub is
unreachable. It raises `FileNotFoundError` when neither the cache nor
the repo has a `.litertlm` file.
[`cached_model`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#cached_model)
is the cache step on its own. It returns the cached path, or None,
without using the network. The old names `_get_model` and
`_cached_model` still work.

[`LitertChat.create_engine`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#litertchat.create_engine)
builds the engine. Unless you name a backend, it tries the GPU first and
falls back to the CPU with a warning. Set `RISHI_LITERT_GPU=0` to skip
the GPU attempt. Pass `backend=Backend.GPU()` or `backend=Backend.CPU()`
to choose the hardware. On the GPU, activations default to 32-bit
floats. With `multimodal=True`, the default, it also builds the vision
and audio encoders that the model file contains. `vision_backend` and
`audio_backend` choose their hardware, CPU by default. A backend named
for an encoder the file lacks gives a warning. `cache_dir` is the
LiteRT-LM cache directory. rishi creates it if it is missing.

`think=True` turns thinking on. `filter_think`, on by default, keeps the
thought tokens out of the key-value cache (KV cache), where LiteRT-LM
stores the keys and values computed for earlier tokens. `constrain`
switches on constrained decoding, which keeps tool calls well formed. It
defaults to on when the chat has tools. `parallel_tools=True` raises
`NotImplementedError`, because the engine’s loop runs one call at a
time. If the context window fills during a turn, the chat drops messages
from the middle of the history, rebuilds the conversation and sends the
turn again. It keeps the first 2 and the last 6 messages. It raises
`ContextWindowExceededError` when nothing can be dropped.

The constants below are the Gemma 4 builds from `litert-community`.

## Recorded model behaviour

These checks run against replies recorded from the real `gemma4_e2b`
model. Urai’s `CachedChat` replays a recorded reply when it sees the
same request again, without loading the model. Each check opens a fresh
`CachedChat`, and they work on a temporary copy of `nbs/chatcache` so
the recordings stay unchanged. They cover one turn, a second turn, a
changed system prompt, a one-shot call, a prompt too long for the
context window, and a tool call that LiteRT-LM ran itself.

``` python
# A normal turn records the response and canonical history produced by LiteRT.
c = CachedChat(**_litert_record_kw)
r = c('Reply with exactly: pong')
test_eq(resp_text(r), 'pong')
test_eq(c.hist, [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'Reply with exactly: pong'},
                 {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'pong'}])
c.close()
```

``` python
# A second turn sees the first through LiteRT's conversation history.
c = CachedChat(**_litert_record_kw)
c('Reply with exactly: pong')
r = c('What exact word did you just reply with? Reply with only that word.')
test_eq(resp_text(r), 'pong')
test_eq([m['role'] for m in c.hist], ['user', 'assistant', 'user', 'assistant'])
c.close()
```

``` python
# Reconfiguration reaches the model without retaining state from another check.
c = CachedChat(**_litert_record_kw)
c.reconfigure(sp='Reply with exactly the word anchor, whatever the user asks.')
r = c('What is two plus two?')
test_eq(resp_text(r), 'anchor')
c.close()
```

``` python
# One-shots use a throwaway LiteRT conversation and do not change history.
c = CachedChat(**_litert_record_kw)
test_eq(c.oneshot('Reply with exactly: solo', think=False, max_tokens=16), 'solo')
test_eq(c.hist, [])
c.close()
```

``` python
# Tool history comes from a real native LiteRT tool round.
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    "Add two integers."
    return a + b

c = CachedChat(**_litert_record_kw, tools=[add])
r = c('Use the add tool to add 2 and 3. Reply with only the result.')
test_eq(resp_text(c.hist[1]), '')
test_eq(c.hist[1]['tool_calls'][0]['function']['name'], 'add')
test_eq(c.hist[2]['role'], 'tool')
test_eq(c.hist[2]['content'], '5.0')
assert '5' in resp_text(r)
c.close()
```

``` python
# fmt2hist / hist2fmt round-trip (model-free)
_nat = [
    'hi',
    Message.model(Contents.of('hello')).to_json(),
    {'role': 'model', 'tool_calls': [{'type': 'function', 'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 2, 'b': 3}}}]},
    {'role': 'tool', 'content': [{'type': 'tool_response', 'name': 'add', 'response': 5}]},
]
_canon = LitertChat.fmt2hist(_nat)
test_eq(_canon[0], {'role': 'user', 'content': 'hi'})
test_eq(_canon[1], {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'hello'})
test_eq(_canon[2]['role'], 'assistant')
test_eq(_canon[2]['tool_calls'][0]['function'], {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 2, 'b': 3}})
assert _canon[2]['tool_calls'][0]['id']                       # a synthetic id was assigned
test_eq(_canon[3], {'role': 'tool', 'name': 'add', 'content': '5'})

# canonical -> litert Messages ready for the engine
_ms = LitertChat.hist2fmt(_canon)
test_eq([m.role for m in _ms], [Role.USER, Role.MODEL, Role.MODEL, Role.TOOL])
test_eq(str(_ms[1]), 'hello')
test_eq(_ms[2].tool_calls[0].name, 'add')
test_eq(_ms[3].contents.to_json(), [{'type': 'tool_response', 'name': 'add', 'response': '5'}])

# fmt2hist is idempotent on an already-canonical (llama-origin) tool round
_llama = [{'role': 'assistant', 'content': '', 'tool_calls': [{'id': 'call_x', 'type': 'function',
                                                               'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 1}}}]},
          {'role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': 'call_x', 'name': 'add', 'content': '1'}]
test_eq(LitertChat.fmt2hist(_llama), _llama)
```

When the window fills after a tool round, the rebuilt conversation keeps
only history from before the turn and the turn message is sent again. A
stream closed early cancels the native generation.

``` python
# Chats sharing one engine take turns on it (model-free)
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace
def _free(lock):
    "Whether another thread could take `lock` right now."
    out = []
    def _try():
        ok = lock.acquire(blocking=False); out.append(ok)
        if ok: lock.release()
    t = threading.Thread(target=_try); t.start(); t.join()
    return out[0]
def _chat(eng, **kw): return SimpleNamespace(engine=eng, cbs=L(), _budget_exceeded=False, max_steps=None, _steps=0, approve=None, hist=[], tool_max_len=None, **kw)
_eng = SimpleNamespace(); _lk = engine_lock(_eng)
assert engine_lock(_eng) is _lk and _free(_lk)

# Two threads: sends never overlap
_log = []
def _send(ch, tag):
    with EngineHold(ch): _log.append((tag, 'in')); time.sleep(0.05); _log.append((tag, 'out'))
_ts = [threading.Thread(target=_send, args=(_chat(_eng), t)) for t in 'ab']
for t in _ts: t.start()
for t in _ts: t.join()
test_eq([x[1] for x in _log], ['in', 'out', 'in', 'out'])
assert _free(_lk)

# One thread, two streams: the second fails fast instead of hanging the thread that holds the first
def _stream(ch):
    with EngineHold(ch): yield 1; yield 2
_c1, _c2 = _chat(_eng), _chat(_eng)
_a = _stream(_c1); next(_a)
_b = _stream(_c2)
test_fail(lambda: next(_b), contains='mid-turn on this engine')
_a.close(); assert _free(_lk)
test_eq(list(_stream(_c2)), [1, 2]); assert _free(_lk)   # `_b` died with the error; a fresh stream gets in

# A stream abandoned on another thread frees the engine when closed from this one
_box = []
_t = threading.Thread(target=lambda: (_box.append(_stream(_chat(_eng))), next(_box[0]))); _t.start(); _t.join()
assert not _free(_lk)
_box[0].close(); assert _free(_lk)

# An exception mid-stream lets go
def _bad(ch):
    with EngineHold(ch): yield 1; raise ValueError('boom')
_g = _bad(_c1); next(_g); test_fail(lambda: next(_g), contains='boom'); assert _free(_lk)

# The same chat, deeper in its own turn (recover_context, a one-shot from a callback), gets straight in
with EngineHold(_c1):
    with EngineHold(_c1): assert not _free(_lk)
    assert not _free(_lk)
assert _free(_lk)

# The tool loop lets go while a tool runs, so a tool may use the engine, and takes it back for the reply
_ch = _chat(_eng); _ch._hold, _th = EngineHold(_ch), ChatToolHandler(_ch)
with _ch._hold:
    assert not _free(_lk)
    assert _th.approve_tool_call({'function': {'name': 'add', 'arguments': {'a': 2, 'b': 3}}})
    assert _free(_lk)
    with EngineHold(_c2): pass                       # another chat on this thread, from inside the tool
    test_eq(_th.process_tool_response('5'), '5')
    assert not _free(_lk)
assert _free(_lk)
test_eq([m['role'] for m in _ch.hist], ['assistant', 'tool'])
_ch._hold.let_go(); assert _free(_lk)           # letting go twice is harmless
```

``` python
class _FakeConv:
    token_count = 0
    cancelled = 0
    def send_message(self, m, **kw): return {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'ok'}
    def send_message_async(self, m, **kw): yield from [{'i': 0}, {'i': 1}]
    def cancel_process(self): self.cancelled += 1

class _FakeTurn:
    _sys_pre, turn_msg, _turn_msg_recorded, conv, _hold, cbs = [], 'q', True, _FakeConv(), ExitStack(), L()
    def __init__(self):
        self.hist = [{'role': 'user', 'content': f'm{i}'} for i in range(14)]
        self.hist += [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'q'}, {'role': 'assistant', 'content': '', 'tool_calls': [{'id': '1'}]},
                      {'role': 'tool', 'tool_call_id': '1', 'content': 'r'}]
    def _mk_conv(self, msgs): self.rebuilt = msgs
    def _turn_kw(self, kw): return {}
    def add_cbs(self, cbs): return []
    def remove_cbs(self, added): pass
    def _emit(self, o, fmt): return o

t = _FakeTurn()
LitertChat._retry_evicted(t, RuntimeError('ctx'))
rebuilt = [m.to_json() for m in t.rebuilt]
test_eq({m['role'] for m in rebuilt}, {'user'})
test_eq([m['content'] for m in t.hist[-2:]], ['m13', 'q'])

s = LitertChat._stream(t, 'hi'); next(s); s.close()
test_eq(t.conv.cancelled, 1)
list(LitertChat._stream(t, 'hi'))
test_eq(t.conv.cancelled, 1)
[m['content'] for m in t.hist]
```

``` python
# Real LiteRT conversation-cache test. BenchmarkInfo reports the actual last prefill performed by
# the runtime; turn two should prefill only its short new message while retaining the old KV context.
kvchat = Chat(backend=Backend.GPU(), cache_dir='.cache/litertlm', think=False, max_output_tokens=16,
              eng_kw={'enable_benchmark': True})
try:
    kvchat(('cache verification context ' * 96) + '\nReply with exactly: stored')
    first = kvchat.conv.get_benchmark_info()
    context_before_turn2 = kvchat.token_count
    r = kvchat('What exact word did I ask you to reply with? Reply with only that word.')
    second = kvchat.conv.get_benchmark_info()
    print(dict(first_prefill=first.last_prefill_token_count,
               second_prefill=second.last_prefill_token_count,
               context_before_turn2=context_before_turn2,
               context_after_turn2=kvchat.token_count,
               reported_cached=kvchat.use.cached_tokens,
               answer=resp_text(r)))
    assert context_before_turn2 > 0 and kvchat.token_count > context_before_turn2
    assert second.last_prefill_token_count < context_before_turn2, 'turn two appears to have re-prefilled the old context'
    assert kvchat.use.cached_tokens == context_before_turn2, kvchat.use
    assert 'stored' in resp_text(r).lower(), resp_text(r)
finally:
    kvchat.close()
```

### Images and audio

Gemma 4 builds take images and audio next to the text in one call, in
the same list form as the other backends. The second call passes a
LiteRT-LM `AudioFile` directly, which also works.

``` python
from PIL import Image
from fastcore.all import img_bytes, Path
from rishi.core import repo_root
im = Image.open(repo_root()/'nbs'/'images.jpeg')
chat(['explain this image', img_bytes(im)])
chat(['transcribe this audio', AudioFile(str(repo_root()/'nbs'/'speech.wav'))])
```

>

>
> 1.  **Analyze the Request:** The user has provided an audio
>     transcription and wants me to transcribe it.

## Utilities and bench

`classify`, `structured` and `check` come from Urai and work here as on
every backend. The example below classifies a sentence and extracts a
dataclass from another.
[`bench()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#bench) is
particular to LiteRT-LM. It runs LiteRT-LM’s `Benchmark` on a model and
reports the load time, the time to the first token, and the prefill and
decode speeds in tokens per second. It uses the CPU backend and 64
prefill and 64 decode tokens unless you pass `backend`, `prefill_tokens`
or `decode_tokens`. This backend has no log-likelihood scoring.
LiteRT-LM cannot score how likely a given text is.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi/blob/main/rishi/litert.py#L513"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    model_id:str='litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm', model_path:NoneType=None,
    backend:litert_lm.interfaces.CPU=CPU(thread_count=None), prefill_tokens:int=64, decode_tokens:int=64, **kw
):
```

*Measure a model’s load time, time to first token, and prefill and
decode speed with LiteRT-LM’s `Benchmark`.*

``` python
# classify + structured on a real model
sm = Chat(cache_dir='.cache/litertlm')
test_eq(sm.classify("I absolutely loved this film!", ['positive', 'negative']), 'positive')

from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass
class Person: name:str; age:int
p = sm.structured("Extract the person: John Smith is 30 years old.", Person)
print(p); assert isinstance(p, Person) and 'John' in p.name
sm.close()
```

    Person(name='John Smith', age=30)

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
import rishi.litert
test_eq(get_runtime('litert'), rishi.litert.LitertChat)

# dispatch really happens in `Chat.__new__`, so it can be checked without loading a model
test_eq(type(Chat.__new__(Chat)), rishi.litert.LitertChat)              # the default runtime
test_eq(type(Chat.__new__(Chat, 'litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm')),
        rishi.litert.LitertChat)
test_eq(rishi.litert.LitertChat._runtime, 'litert')
```

## Sharing one engine

A LiteRT-LM `Engine` lives inside one process, so separate programs
cannot attach to it.
[`LitertBroker`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#litertbroker)
keeps one in a long-lived process and serves a
[`LitertChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rishi/litert.html#litertchat)
to each client over a Unix socket. Each client has its own conversation
and history, and all of them share one copy of the weights. Turns run
one at a time, because one engine cannot be driven from two threads at
once. The protocol is Urai’s `ChatBroker`, described on Urai’s
[broker](https://vedicreader.github.io/urai/broker.html) page.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi/blob/main/rishi/litert.py#L519"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>
